name: pediatric seizures overview
title: A child with a seizure: ABCDE and a bedside glucose and blood gas for every child, then fever and the seizure's features sort a simple from a complex febrile seizure, and a seizure past 5 minutes is convulsive status epilepticus treated by the clock with benzodiazepines, then a second-line load, then the intensive care unit, and then its causes by age and the treatment of each cause

root.title: Child seizing: ABCDE + time it
lines: Airway: bag-mask, laryngeal mask or tube if needed · Circulation: early fast pulse, high BP tolerated, LOW BP → fluid bolus
Disability: pupils (dilated or pinpoint → overdose · blown or fixed → raised pressure, bleed) · glucose · Exposure: safe space, skin
EVERY child: bedside GLUCOSE + blood GAS with electrolytes
history: onset, timing, duration · movements, eyes, focal or generalized · consciousness during and after, recovery · fever, trauma, toxins, drugs or withdrawal · milestones, family epilepsy
exam: vitals · pupils, cranial nerves, tone, reflexes, focal deficits · raised pressure (bulging fontanelle, papilledema) · café au lait spots (neurofibromatosis)
subtle in newborns: lip smacking, sucking, chewing, eye deviation or fluttering, bicycling, apnea, vital sign changes · subclinical: EEG only

groups.title: FEVER, age 6 months-5 years: FEBRILE seizure
lines: only if NO CNS infection, NO acute electrolyte problem, NO past afebrile seizure
WORRY: not back to baseline · meningeal signs or toxic look · delay or neurologic condition

groups.title: Still seizing at 5 MINUTES
lines: or no return to baseline between seizures

head: h
Simple febrile seizure
pres: fever · generalized tonic-clonic 3 min · now alert, playful
inv: if back to baseline, no other concern

head: h
Complex febrile seizure
pres: 2 right-sided seizures (4 min) in one day · now normal
inv: by time back to baseline, neurologic signs, family comfort
tx: counsel: can recur and become epilepsy

head: h
Convulsive status epilepticus
> 30 min, or 2+ seizures without recovery
10-73 per 100,000 children a year · most under 2
pres: • longer = ↑ brain oxygen demand, cell death: time matters
• 3, no past seizures, convulsing 10 min → status
• 2-day newborn: lip smacking, eye deviation, apnea, not stopped by 2 lorazepam, glucose normal → PHENOBARBITAL
inv: • infection: blood count, CRP, cultures, CSF if stable
• head CT: head injury, focal signs, raised pressure (pupils, high BP + slow pulse, vomiting, lethargy)
tx: • no IV access: sublingual lorazepam or intranasal midazolam
cause: • missed or stopped anti-seizure drug, overdose
triggers: fever, dehydration, missed drug, toxins
• infection in utero or at birth
fix: • rule of 50: D10 5 mL/kg (or D5 10 mL/kg)
• D25, D50 NOT peripheral: thrombosis, phlebitis
